title: Aerogel cost reduction for building insulation
bottleneck: Silica aerogels insulate better than any conventional material, but supercritical drying — needed to preserve their nanoporous structure — is slow, energy-intensive, and batch-limited, keeping prices near $100 per square meter versus cents for fiberglass. Ambient-pressure drying routes collapse pores unless expensive surface treatments are used, and the resulting blankets are fragile and dusty. No process yet delivers aerogel performance near conventional insulation cost.
why_it_blocks: Buildings consume about a third of global energy, much of it for heating and cooling through poorly insulated envelopes. Aerogel pricing keeps super-insulation out of mainstream construction, forcing reliance on thicker conventional insulation that steals floor space and still underperforms.
current_state: Ambient-dried aerogel blankets have reached the market for industrial and niche building uses at falling prices, and production scale-up continues. But the order-of-magnitude cost gap to mass-market insulation persists, and fragility limits handling on real job sites.
